knowledgeImport.title: Bring my knowledge
knowledgeImport.description: Bring what ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity already know about your work. You choose what Cendr keeps, and where.
knowledgeImport.videoSoonBody: Meanwhile, the steps for each tool appear below when you choose it.
knowledgeImport.privacyTitle: Your knowledge, not your private life.
knowledgeImport.privacyBody: Cendr analyses your files to find the knowledge and preferences that help your work. Sensitive personal information is kept out of memory and personalisation, and nothing enters them without your approval. You stay in control of what is kept and shared.
knowledgeImport.how1: Your archive is opened in your browser: it is neither uploaded nor kept as such on our side.
knowledgeImport.how2: Only the text you wrote (not the assistants' answers, not attachments) is sent, in small batches, to our server to be sorted. PDF and Word files are read on our server, in memory, without being kept.
knowledgeImport.how3: Our server first removes, without AI, the conversations and passages about health, love life, family, politics, religion or personal money, and any password, key or bank number. Remaining names and contact details are masked.
knowledgeImport.how4: Your company's AI model then proposes the useful knowledge. Each proposal is checked a second time, then you approve, edit or refuse it. Refused, it is deleted at once.
knowledgeImport.how5: Proposals not reviewed are deleted after {days} days. Nothing is written to our logs.
knowledgeImport.howLimit: This sorting relies on word lists and rules: it greatly reduces what gets through, but cannot guarantee that nothing personal slips by. That is why you approve every proposal.
knowledgeImport.chooseSource: Where does your knowledge come from?

guide.auto: Choose your former tool to see how to export your data, or drop your file directly: Cendr recognises ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity.
guide.chatgpt: In ChatGPT: Settings → Data controls → Export data. You receive an e-mail with a link to a .zip file (it can take up to 24 hours). Drop that .zip here as it is.
guide.claude: In Claude: Settings → Privacy → Export data. You receive an e-mail with a .zip file. Drop it here as it is. Your projects' instructions are kept; their documents are not.
guide.gemini: On takeout.google.com: select only "My Activity", then in its options keep only "Gemini Apps" (JSON format if offered). Drop the .zip you receive here.
guide.perplexity: Perplexity has no full export: open a conversation, then export it as Markdown or PDF. Drop one or several files here.
guide.files: Notes and documents: Markdown, text, HTML, CSV, PDF or Word, alone or in a .zip.

google.body: Gmail, Calendar, Drive (Docs and Sheets included).
google.limits: Gmail and Drive are "restricted" permissions at Google: the Cendr app must pass Google's security verification before it is open to everyone. Docs and Sheets are read as text (formatting not kept); Cendr does not edit them.

microsoft.body: Outlook (mail and calendar), OneDrive and SharePoint (Word, Excel, PowerPoint files), Teams.
microsoft.limits: Posting in Teams often needs a Microsoft 365 administrator's consent. PowerPoint files are not read as text; Word, Excel, PDF and text are. Microsoft offers no remote revocation for one app: Cendr deletes its keys, and the person can remove Cendr from their Microsoft account.

slack.limits: Cendr only reads public channels its app was added to. No private messages.

notion.limits: Cendr only reaches the pages you share with it when connecting (or later in Notion). Text is read without nested databases.

canva.limits: Canva's API cannot write content into a design (except brand templates to fill, reserved to Canva Enterprise): Cendr creates an empty design to complete in Canva.
